title: SLO Anchoring and Debt Amnesty Runbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This runbook defines the SLO anchoring and Error Budget Amnesty process for Redwood Inference services. It codifies how teams anchor SLOs, measure and bank error budget, and execute temporary amnesty windows to remediate long-standing capacity or reliability debt without immediate customer-facing SLO rollbacks. The runbook includes decision criteria, automation recipes, operational steps for oncall during breaches, and the governance cycle for debt forgiveness.

Scope:
- Applies to all public-facing inference and control-plane services managed by eng-sre and service owners.
- Excludes internal CI/CD jobs and transient dev/test environments unless explicitly adopted by the owning team.

Motivation:
Over time, services accumulate reliability and capacity debt (configuration drift, under-provisioned autoscale, legacy quantization profiles, missing caching). SLO Anchoring + Debt Amnesty provides a controlled mechanism to:
- Prevent reactive SLO relaxation as first response.
- Give teams a predictable window to fix root causes with reduced risk of customer impact.
- Preserve long-term trust by requiring evidence and post-mortems for forgiven debt.

Definitions and key terms:
- SLO Anchor: A durable, documented SLO baseline that a service can fall back to in emergency rollback scenarios. Anchors must be reviewed quarterly.
- Error Budget Bank: Numeric ledger recording accumulated unused error budget (positive) or overspend (negative) over a rolling 30d window.
- Debt Amnesty Window: A pre-authorized operational window (normally 8–72 hours) where teams may accept temporary increased SLO risk in order to implement fixes that would otherwise violate immediate SLO constraints.
- SLO Debt: Persistent SLO consumption trends caused by non-transient causes (e.g., design limitations, capacity debt).

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce frequency of permanent SLO rollbacks by 60% year-over-year.
- Execute Debt Amnesty windows with automated guardrails such that customer-visible errors increase less than 3x baseline tail for the window.
- 100% of forgiven debt must have a documented remediation timeline and assigned owner within 5 working days.

SLO Anchoring Process (quarterly cadence)
1. Quarterly Review: Service owners run the SLO Anchoring checklist before each quarterly review.
   - Must verify the anchor SLO, backing dashboards, alert thresholds, and canary test coverage.
2. Choose anchor levels: For each primary SLI (p99 latency, availability, inference-cpu-error-rate) define:
   - Operational SLO: e.g., 99.9% for production requests (business-facing).
   - Anchor SLO: e.g., 99.5% — used for safe rollback and capacity planning.
3. Document anchor in the service README and register in the SLO ledger: team-slo-registry.redwood.internal (see Appendix A sample).
4. Run canary verification: execute synthetic canaries (1000 requests/sec for 10 minutes) against the anchor variant.

Decision criteria for invoking Debt Amnesty
- Preconditions (all required):
  a) A remediation requires actions that will temporarily increase SLO burn (examples: offline shard migration, cache warming by replaying traffic, model re-quantization that temporarily increases tails).
  b) The Error Budget Bank for the service is >= -0.5% (i.e., small deficit allowed) OR cross-team bank approval is granted.
  c) There is a defined remediation plan with owner, rollback plan, and automated guardrails.
- Approvers: service owner + SRE oncall for the owning calendar block + product manager for customer-impacting routes.

Debt Amnesty Window: operational steps (8–72 hour window)
1. Pre-window (24–72 hours before):
   - Submit Debt Amnesty ticket in Jira using template AMN-<service>-<date>. Required fields: expected extra burn %, monitoring dashboard links, runbook, owner, rollback plan, start/end UTC times.
   - Notify oncall and affected customers (if customer-facing SLA) with the planned window and mitigation (email + status page pre-incident notice).
   - Create a canary traffic slice and shadow traffic config.
2. 2 hours before start:
   - Lock autoscaling smoothing to allow planned changes (set smoothing to 5m -> 30s as appropriate).
   - Deploy telemetry checkpoint: configure ephemeral additional tracing and increased metric resolution (1s/10s -> 250ms/1s).
3. During window: continuous monitoring (see guardrails below).
4. Immediately on threshold breach: abort and roll back (automated action).
5. Post-window: collect evidence, run remediation ticket closure checklist, submit postmortem if any customer-visible error >= severity 2.

Guardrails and automatic abort conditions
- Abort triggers (automated):
  - 5-minute p99 latency > 3x baseline AND increase sustained for 5 consecutive minutes.
  - Availability drop causing >= 0.5% absolute drop in daily availability compared to pre-window baseline.
  - Error rate increase causing customer 4xx/5xx spike > 2x baseline or synthetic canary failure rate > 1%.
- Automated actions on abort:
  - Revert deployment via rollback script: /opt/deploy/rollback.sh --service <svc> --to-last-stable \\n  - Raise PagerDuty with tag amnesty_abort and execute emergency shim (move traffic to anchor pool).

Error Budget Bank model (ledger)
- Rolling window: 30d for short-lived services, 90d for long-lived heavy-state services.
- Bank entries are recorded as percentage points of SLO per day and summarized weekly.
- Positive bank: unused error budget carried forward until consumed.
- Negative bank: small deficits allowed up to -1.0% for 30d with escalations.

Sample ledger table (text):
| Date | Service | Delta (SLO pts) | Reason | Owner | Notes |
|------|---------|----------------|--------|-------|-------|
| 2026-02-12 | inference-api-prod | +0.08% | Low tail on new quarter | Maya Patel | carried |
| 2026-02-24 | control-plane | -0.45% | Migration prep spike | Diego Alvarez | amnesty requested |

Runbook for active breach during Amnesty window (oncall steps)
1. Triage: confirm which SLI is violating.
2. Verify automation logs: run "/usr/local/bin/amnesty-check --svc <svc> --window-id <id>" to get golden signals and check abort conditions.
3. If abort trigger fired: run rollback: "/opt/deploy/rollback.sh --service <svc> --to-last-stable" and escalate to senior SRE.
4. If within guardrails: keep remediation running and increase telemetry collection.
5. Always update the Jira ticket with timestamps for any aborts, mitigations, or customer communications.

Roles and responsibilities
- Service Owner: documents remediation, responsible for follow-up and backlog items.
- Oncall SRE: approves the window, watches the guardrails, executes aborts.
- Reliability Program Manager: maintains the Error Budget Bank summary and approves cross-team debt forgiveness.
- Product Manager: approves any customer-facing risk.

Automation and operational tooling (concrete examples)
- Dashboards: SLO-Amnesty-<service> dashboard (Grafana): panels for p50/p95/p99, error-rate, synthetic canary, anchor-pool-traffic.
- Prometheus queries (examples):
  - p99 latency (1m):
    histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))
  - error rate (5m):
    sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
- Automation scripts:
  - Amnesty check CLI (runs in CI):
    #!/bin/bash
    svc=$1
    window=$2
    curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/amnesty-check?svc=$svc&window=$window" | jq '.'
- CI job: scheduled amnesty validation job (Jenkins/GitHub Actions) that runs pre-window canaries and uploads a snapshot to the ticket.

Communications template (short)
- Incident channel message (pre-window):
  [AMN] <service> scheduled debt amnesty window starting <start> UTC — owner <name>. Expected elevated tail for up to <hours>. Guardrails configured: p99 abort 3x baseline, error-rate abort 2x.
- Customer notice (if required): short description, start/end, mitigation contact, link to status page.

Post-amnesty governance and audit
- Within 5 business days: service owner posts remediation backlog with owners and ETA.
- Within 10 business days: reliability program manager reviews and verifies that work is scheduled.
- Every forgiven debt entry requires a 1-page short postmortem (root cause + permanent fix + timeline).
- Repeated amnesty use (>3 per quarter) triggers a reliability review board.

Risk matrix and decision table (text):
1) Low-risk tasks (cache warm, config tuning): allow self-serve amnesty if bank >= 0.0% and SRE oncall notified.
2) Medium-risk (shard migration, model swap with compatibility risk): require SRE approval and PM signoff, bank >= -0.5% or cross-team approval.
3) High-risk (database schema changes, network fabric maintenance): disallowed under amnesty; use scheduled maintenance with customer communication.

Appendix A: sample SLO registry entry (YAML)
---
service: inference-api-prod
primary_sli: availability
slo: "99.9%"
anchor_slo: "99.5%"
rolling_window_days: 30
contact: eng-inference@redwood.internal
owner: Maya Patel
last_reviewed: "2026-03-01"
---

Appendix B: common commands
- Trigger pre-window canary: "make canary-run SERVICE=inference-api-prod DURATION=10m"
- Check amnesty status: "/usr/local/bin/amnesty-check --svc inference-api-prod --window 2026-03-10T00:00Z"
- Force abort (when automation fails): "/opt/deploy/rollback.sh --service inference-api-prod --force"

Appendix C: templates
- Jira template fields (short):
  - Summary: Debt Amnesty request - <service> - <start>
  - Description: Expected actions, risk, rollback, monitoring links, owner
  - Labels: amnesty, <service>, srl
